questions.question: Competitive behaviour and competitive market structure are _______ related.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**inversely**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Competitive behaviour and competitive market structure** are **inversely**__ related.
 
• As the market structure becomes more competitive, the intensity of competitive behaviour among firms tends to decrease.
 
• Conversely, in less competitive market structures, firms are likely to exhibit more aggressive competitive behaviours to gain a larger market share.
 
• This inverse relationship is crucial in understanding market dynamics and the strategic interactions between firms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of market structure and competitive behaviour is fundamental in the field of **industrial organization**.
 
• Market structures can range from **perfect competition** to **monopoly**, with various forms of oligopoly and monopolistic competition in between.
 
• In a perfectly competitive market, firms are price takers and have minimal competitive behaviour regarding pricing.
 
• In contrast, in a monopolistic market, the single firm has significant market power and competitive behaviour can involve barriers to entry and other strategic actions.
 
• Understanding the relationship between market structure and competitive behaviour helps in **regulating markets** and promoting fair competition.

questions.question: If ex ante aggregate demand and ex ante aggregate supply are plotted together in a graphical diagram, then at which point equilibrium will be reached?

options.text: Where ex ante aggregate demand is less than ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is equal to ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is more than ex ante aggregate supply
Where ex ante aggregate demand is zero

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__**.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** In a graphical diagram where ex ante aggregate demand (AD) and ex ante aggregate supply (AS) are plotted together, equilibrium is reached at the point where the two curves intersect.**
 
• This intersection represents the level of real output and price level where** the quantity of goods and services demanded (AD) is equal to the quantity supplied (AS).**
 
• **At this equilibrium point**, there is no tendency for the economy to move away from it, as the quantity demanded matches the quantity supplied.
 
• **The equilibrium point** can be thought of as the point of balance in the economy, where there is no excess demand or excess supply.
 
• It is where **buyers' and sellers' **plans align, resulting in a stable state in which the economy is in equilibrium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In an economy, demand and supply refer to the forces that determine the quantity** **of goods and services exchanged in the market. **

 
 
• **Demand: **Demand represents the quantity of goods and services that buyers are willing and able to purchase at various price levels, during a specific period.

 
 
• Demand is influenced by factors such as price, consumer preferences, income levels, population, and the availability of substitutes.
 
• The relationship between price and quantity demanded is typically inverse, meaning that as the price increases, the quantity demanded tends to decrease, and vice versa.
 
• Demand is usually represented by a downward-sloping demand curve.
 
 
 
• **Supply: **Supply, on the other hand, represents the quantity of goods and services that sellers are willing and able to offer for sale at different price levels.
 
 
• The supply is influenced by factors such as production costs, technology, resource availability, government regulations, and expectations of future prices.
 
• The relationship between price and quantity supplied is usually positive, meaning that as the price increases, the quantity supplied tends to increase, and vice versa.
 
• Supply is often represented by an upward-sloping supply curve.
 
 
 
• **The interaction of demand and supply determines** **the equilibrium price** **and quantity in a market.**
 
 
• When the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied, the market is said to be in equilibrium.
 
• Changes in demand or supply will shift the respective curves, leading to changes in the equilibrium price and quantity.
 
• For example, an increase in demand will shift the demand curve to the right, leading to a higher equilibrium price and quantity.
 
 
 
 
 
• Understanding the dynamics of demand and supply is crucial in analyzing market behavior, price fluctuations, and the allocation of resources in an economy.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true with respect to MRTP Act?

i) The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act) was repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.

ii) The asset limit for MRTP companies was fixed at Rs. 25 crores by the first/original Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act).

iii) The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act) was first passed in 1969.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only i and iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• i) **True**: The MRTP Act was indeed repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, which aimed to promote and sustain competition in the markets.
 
• ii) **False**: The original asset limit for MRTP companies **was set at Rs. 20 crores, not Rs. 25 crores.**
 
• iii)**True**: The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 to prevent monopolistic and restrictive trade practices.
 
• Thus, **statements i and iii are true** with respect to the MRTP Act.

questions.question: Following are the industry categories classified under the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, EXCEPT:

options.text: industries with public sector taking the lead and the private sector playing a supplementary role
industries with exclusive ownership of the state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** industries in the cooperative sector.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution 1956:-**

 
 
• **It was a policy framework for the development of industries in India.**
 
• The policy classified industries into three categories: (1) industries in the private sector, (2) industries with the public sector taking the lead and the private sector playing a supplementary role, and (3) industries with exclusive ownership of the state.
 
• The** policy did not include industries in the cooperative sector** as a separate category.
 
• The cooperative sector refers to businesses that are owned and operated by **a group of individuals who share the profits and control the operations.**
 
• ** The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 was replaced by the New Industrial Policy in 1991, which encouraged liberalization, privatization, and globalization of industries in India.**
 
• **Highlights of IPR 1956:**
 
 
• In order to initiate a new industry or expand existing capacity, private entrepreneurs were supposed to obtain licenses from the government.
 
• Licensing, imposition of the tax, tax exemptions, and subsidies were used by the government:
 
 
• to regulate private industries.
 
• bring about a reduction in regional disparities in industrial development. 
 
• to keep a check on the production of goods that are socially undesirable.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industries with public sector taking the lead and the private sector playing a supplementary role:-**

 
 
• It refers to industries where the government takes the lead in ownership and management, and the private sector plays a supportive role.
 
• This model was adopted for industries such as steel, coal, and power generation.
 
 
 
• **Industries in the private sector:-**
 
 
• It refers to industries that are owned and operated by private individuals or companies. This model was encouraged for industries such as consumer goods, textiles, and services.
 
 
 
• **Industries with exclusive ownership of the state:-**
 
 
• It refers to industries that are wholly owned and operated by the state. This model was adopted for industries such as defense, atomic energy, and railways.

options.text: Those living below poverty line get food grains at subsidised prices.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Public distribution system (PDS) is an Indian food Security System** established under the **Ministry of Consumer Affairs**, **Food, and Public Distribution**.
 
• It evolved as a system of management of scarcity through the distribution of food grains at affordable prices.
 
• It is operated under the** joint responsibility of the Central and the State Governments**.
 
• Under the PDS, presently the commodities namely wheat, rice, sugar, and kerosene are being allocated to the States/UTs for distribution.
 
• Some states/UTs also distribute additional items of mass consumption through the PDS outlets such as pulses, edible oils, iodized salt, spices, etc.
 
• From the 1970s, it had evolved into a **universal scheme for the distribution of subsidized food.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

• In June 1997, the Government of India launched the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) with a focus on the poor.
 
• Under TPDS, beneficiaries were divided into two categories:
 
 
• Households below the poverty line or BPL
 
• Households above the poverty line or APL.

questions.question: When was air transport nationalised in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1953**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Air transport was nationalized in India in the year **1953**.
 
• The Government of India passed the **Air Corporations Act, 1953**, which led to the nationalization of the airline industry.
 
• Two new corporations, **Air India International** and **Indian Airlines**, were established to handle international and domestic air services, respectively.
 
• This move was aimed at ensuring better management, safety, and growth of the aviation sector in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Air Corporations Act, 1953**, was repealed in 1994, paving the way for private airlines to operate in India.
 
• Before nationalization, there were several private airlines operating in India, including Tata Airlines, which later became Air India.
 
• Nationalization helped in standardizing operations and improving the safety record of Indian aviation.
 
• Today, the Indian aviation sector is a mix of public and private enterprises, with numerous domestic and international players.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the fall out of the industrial licensing system?

options.text: Large industrial houses availed licenses to prevent competition
Most licenses were used up by backward states
Most licenses were for importing goods
Many small private firms appropriated licenses

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Large industrial houses availed licenses to prevent competition.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The industrial licensing system in India had several fallout, including:**

 
 
• Large industrial houses availed licenses to prevent competition: The licensing system was often manipulated by big business houses to prevent new players from entering the market, thereby limiting competition.
 
• Most licenses were used up by backward states: The licensing system favored the established industrial centers, and backward states had a tough time getting licenses.
 
• Most licenses were for importing goods: The licensing system was designed to promote domestic manufacturing, and imports were discouraged.
 
• Many small private firms appropriated licenses: The licensing system was biased towards large industrial houses, and small private firms had a tough time getting licenses. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial licensing system:**

 
 
• The industrial licensing system was introduced in India in 1948 to regulate the growth and development of industries in the country.
 
• Under this system, the government issued licenses to companies to set up new industries, expand existing ones, or import technology and machinery.
 
• The licensing system was aimed at achieving a balanced regional development of industries, promoting self-sufficiency, and preventing concentration of economic power in a few hands.
 
• However, the licensing system was often criticized for being bureaucratic, corrupt, and favoring established players over new entrants.
 
• The system was gradually dismantled in the 1990s as part of economic liberalization and reforms.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the direct outcomes that can be attributed to a good industrial sector?

options.text: Provision of mass consumption manufactured goods

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doubling of farmers’ income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Doubling of farmers' income,"** is not directly related to the** industrial sector**. 
 
• Increasing farmers' income typically involves agricultural policies, improvements in farming techniques, infrastructure development in rural areas, and market reforms to ensure fair prices for agricultural products. 
 
• While industrialization may indirectly contribute to overall economic growth and development, specifically doubling farmers' income is not a direct outcome attributed to the industrial sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• The industrial sector primarily focuses on manufacturing goods and providing employment opportunities in factories and production facilities.
 
• The outcomes typically associated with a strong industrial sector include:
 
 
• **Provision of relatively stable employment: **A robust industrial sector often leads to the creation of jobs in manufacturing industries, providing stable employment opportunities for workers.
 
• **Promotion of modernization: **Industrialization drives technological advancements and promotes modernization by encouraging the adoption of new production techniques, machinery, and processes.
 
• **Provision of mass consumption manufactured goods:** A well-developed industrial sector produces a wide range of manufactured goods, including consumer products, which are essential for meeting the demands of the population and driving economic growth through increased consumption.

(b) There is no excess supply in the market

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The market attains equilibrium when the market supply and market demand of a commodity become equal.
 
• The term supply refers to how much of a certain product, item, commodity, or service suppliers are willing to make available at a particular price
 
• Demand refers to how much of that product, item, commodity, or service consumers are willing and able to purchase at a particular price
 
• Supply and demand are economic forces of the free market that control what suppliers are willing to produce and what consumers are willing and able to purchase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the market price is above the equilibrium value, there is an excess supply in the market (a surplus), which means there is more supply than demand.
 
• If the market price is below the equilibrium value, then there is an excess in demand (supply shortage).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9042c9dca25efe9625d51e525814238bd7e86f2da7945bd56a70fc82bed307ae.png]

questions.question: When was the Direct Tax Code Bill introduced in the Parliament of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2010.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **12 August 2009**, the first draft of the **Direct Tax Code Bill **was created.
 
• **In 2010, a Revised Discussion Paper was created.**
 
• **In 2010, The Direct Tax Code bill was introduced in Parliament,** and a Standing Committee of Finance (SCF) was appointed for a detailed discussion.
 
• In 2012, the committee submitted its report to Parliament.
 
• In 2014, a revised version of the Direct Tax Code was created after the committee report.
 
• The bill lapsed due to the change in government after the general elections.
 
• **In 2017**, An expert committee was set up to draft a fresh Direct Tax Code.
 
• In Aug 2019, the task force report was submitted to the Finance Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Tax Type
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Income Tax
 A tax on the income earned by individuals, HUFs, companies, and other entities.
 
 

 Goods and Services Tax (GST)
 A value-added tax on the supply of goods and services, which replaced several indirect taxes such as excise duty, VAT, and service tax.
 
 

 Corporate Tax
 A tax on the profits earned by companies and other business entities.
 
 

 Capital Gains Tax
 A tax on the profits earned from the sale of capital assets such as property, shares, and mutual funds.
 
 

 Wealth Tax
 A tax on the net wealth of individuals and HUFs, which was abolished in 2015.
 
 

 Customs Duty
 A tax on the import and export of goods across India's borders.
 
 

 Excise Duty
 A tax on the production and manufacture of goods within the country.
 
 

 Securities Transaction Tax (STT)
 A tax on the purchase and sale of securities such as stocks, bonds, and mutual funds.
 
 

 Professional Tax
 A tax on the income earned by professionals such as doctors, lawyers, and chartered accountants.
 
 

 Property Tax
 A tax on the ownership or occupation of property, which is levied by local authorities such as municipalities and panchayats.

questions.question: With which of the following is 'Operation Flood' related?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India’s dairy industry.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points:__**

 
• Operation Flood was launched in **1970.**
 
• It was a project of **India's National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).**
 
• It was the world's biggest dairy development program.
 
• In 30 years, it doubled milk available per person, and made dairy farming India's largest self-sustainable rural employment generator.
 
• **Verghese Kurien,** the chairman and founder of Amul, was named the chairman of NDDB by the then Prime Minister of India Lal Bahadur Shastri.
 
 
• He was known as the** father of Operation flood.**

questions.question: Name the campaign launched by the Madhya Pradesh government on the occasion of National Girl Child Day on January 24, 2021, under the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' scheme.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PANKH Abhiyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Pankh campaign,** launched on **National Girl Child Day** on January 24, 2021, is part of the "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" Scheme administered by the Madhya Pradesh Government and spearheaded by Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
 
• PANKH stands for Protection, Awareness of rights, Nutrition, Knowledge, and Health, encapsulating the key pillars essential for the holistic development of girls.
 
• This initiative is dedicated to fostering the overall growth and well-being of the girl child.
 
• Additionally, the Ladli Laxmi Yojana in Madhya Pradesh represents another noteworthy effort aimed at supporting the welfare of girls in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Manjhi Kanya Bhagyashree scheme **was introduced in 2015 by the Women and Child Development Department of Maharashtra. It aims to support the welfare and development of girls in the state.
 
• **Udaan** is a project initiated by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) under the auspices of the Ministry of Human Resource Development, Government of India. 
 
• **The Balika Samriddhi Yojana** is a government program designed to promote the well-being of girls. It provides financial assistance after the birth of a girl child and upon completion of her education, with the objective of combating negative attitudes towards daughters.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) is an employment scheme that was launched in 2005 to provide social security by guaranteeing a minimum of ________ days of paid work per year to all families whose adult members opt for unskilled labour-intensive work.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __100__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) provide 100 days of guaranteed wage employment.
 
• This was initiated with the objective of “enhancing livelihood security in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year, especially to households whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work".
 
• This Act also aims to create durable assets (such as roads, canals, ponds, and wells).
 
• Within 5 km of an applicant’s residence, employment is provided.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**Objectives of MGNREGA:

 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) 
 
• Provide 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to rural unskilled labour
 
• Increase economic security.
 
• Decrease migration of labour from rural to urban areas.
 
• It was known to be the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.
 
• MGNREGA Job Card is a document that renders a worker entitled to work under the MGNREGA scheme.

questions.question: Which group of states was concentrated in the cotton production in the early years to develop textile industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra and Gujarat**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maharashtra and Gujarat** were the states concentrated in cotton production in the early years to develop the textile industry.
 
• The favorable climate and soil conditions in these regions made them ideal for cotton cultivation.
 
• These states were home to some of the earliest and most significant textile mills in India, contributing substantially to the country's textile industry.
 
• The cities of Mumbai (in Maharashtra) and Ahmedabad (in Gujarat) became major centers for the textile industry.
 
• These regions continue to play a crucial role in India's textile sector, which is a significant part of the nation's economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **textile industry** in India is one of the oldest industries and has a strong presence in the national economy.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of cotton and cotton yarn in the world.
 
• The industry provides employment to millions of people, especially in rural areas.
 
• Textile exports are a significant source of foreign exchange earnings for the country.
 
• The Indian government has implemented various policies and schemes to support and promote the textile industry.
